parts.zh: W: 大卫·杰克逊先生是《纽约客》的一名专职撰稿人
M: 人们很容易把注意力集中在挑战上
W: 是的，和年幼的孩子交谈相比
M: 会的，写作方面他们确实会
W: 有没有一些你认为很重要
M: 我的总体想法是广泛阅读
W: 所以，你不像一些家长那样太在意他们阅读的内容？我知道自己对此有些担忧
M: 是的，喜欢读什么就读什么
W: 我觉得，随着孩子步入青春期
M: 我认为，随着他们年龄增长
M：那么，你对未来有什么计划？你打算开一家实体店吗？

items.stem: What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation?

choices.text: He is a staff writer.
choices.zh: 他是一名专职撰稿人。

choices.text: He is an adventurer.
choices.zh: 他是一名冒险家。

choices.text: He is an author of fiction.
choices.zh: 他是一名小说作家。

choices.text: He is a father of four kids.
choices.zh: 他是四个孩子的父亲。

items.stem: What does the man think of young teenagers?

choices.text: They are interested in fairy tales.
choices.zh: 他们对童话故事感兴趣。

choices.text: They are curious and autonomous.
choices.zh: 他们好奇且自主。

choices.text: They are a headache to their parents.
choices.zh: 他们让父母头疼。

choices.text: They are ignorant of politics.
choices.zh: 他们对政治一无所知。

items.stem: How does the man help his kids with their essays?

choices.text: He offers them ample editorial guidance.
choices.zh: 他为他们提供充分的编辑指导。

choices.text: He recommends model essays to them.
choices.zh: 他向他们推荐范文。

choices.text: He gives them encouragement.
choices.zh: 他给予他们鼓励。

choices.text: He teaches them proofreading.
choices.zh: 他教他们校对。

items.stem: What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager?

choices.text: Her tastes in books changed.
choices.zh: 她对书籍的品味发生了变化。

choices.text: She realized the power of reading.
choices.zh: 她意识到了阅读的力量。

choices.text: Her reading opened her eyes to the world.
choices.zh: 她的阅读让她开阔了眼界。

choices.text: She began to perceive the world differently.
choices.zh: 她开始以不同的方式感知世界。

items.stem: What do we learn about the woman?

choices.text: She is a website designer.
choices.zh: 她是一名网站设计师。

choices.text: She is a university graduate.
choices.zh: 她是一名大学毕业生。

choices.text: She is a main street store owner.
choices.zh: 她是一家实体店的店主。

choices.text: She is a successful entrepreneur.
choices.zh: 她是一位成功的企业家。

items.stem: What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first?

choices.text: They were repeatedly rejected by shops.
choices.zh: 它们被商店反复拒绝。

choices.text: They were popular with her classmates.
choices.zh: 它们在她的同学中很受欢迎。

choices.text: They showed her natural talent.
choices.zh: 它们展现了她的天赋。

choices.text: They were mostly failures.
choices.zh: 它们大多是失败之作。

items.stem: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?

choices.text: She had a strong interest in doing it.
choices.zh: 她对做这件事有浓厚的兴趣。

choices.text: She did not like ready-made clothes.
choices.zh: 她不喜欢成衣。

choices.text: She could not find clothes of her size.
choices.zh: 她找不到适合自己尺码的衣服。

choices.text: She found clothes in shops unaffordable.
choices.zh: 她觉得商店里的衣服买不起。

items.stem: What does the woman plan to do in the future?

choices.text: Study fashion design at college.
choices.zh: 在大学学习时装设计。

choices.text: Improve her marketing strategy.
choices.zh: 改进她的营销策略。

choices.text: Add designs for women.
choices.zh: 增加女装设计。

choices.text: Expand her business.
choices.zh: 扩大她的业务。

items.stem: What have researchers done for the first time in history?

choices.text: Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic.
choices.zh: 利用人工智能找到一种强效的新型抗生素。

choices.text: Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
choices.zh: 发现对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的细菌。

choices.text: Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health.
choices.zh: 识别出对人类健康危害最大的细菌菌株。

choices.text: Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic.
choices.zh: 用一种新型抗生素清除人体内的致命细菌菌株。

items.stem: What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs?

choices.text: Ever-increasing strains of bacteria.
choices.zh: 不断增加的细菌菌株。

choices.text: Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
choices.zh: 细菌对抗生素的耐药性。

choices.text: The similarity between known drugs.
choices.zh: 已知药物之间的相似性。

choices.text: The growing threat of bacteria to health.
choices.zh: 细菌对健康日益增长的威胁。

items.stem: What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research?

choices.text: Dispense with experimental testing.
choices.zh: 省去实验性测试。

choices.text: Predict whether compounds are toxic.
choices.zh: 预测化合物是否有毒。

choices.text: Foresee human reaction to antibiotics.
choices.zh: 预见人类对抗生素的反应。

choices.text: Combat bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
choices.zh: 对抗细菌对抗生素的耐药性。

items.stem: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?

choices.text: By theorization.
choices.zh: 通过理论推导。

choices.text: By generalization.
choices.zh: 通过归纳概括。

choices.text: By observation.
choices.zh: 通过观察。

choices.text: By conversation.
choices.zh: 通过交谈。

items.stem: What does the passage say about most lies?

choices.text: They are easy to detect.
choices.zh: 它们很容易识破。

choices.text: They are well intended.
choices.zh: 它们是善意的。

choices.text: They are groundless.
choices.zh: 它们是毫无根据的。

choices.text: They are harmless.
choices.zh: 它们是无害的。

items.stem: What have many studies uncovered about the average person's lie detection?

choices.text: Mostly by chance.
choices.zh: 主要靠运气。

choices.text: Basically objective.
choices.zh: 基本客观。

choices.text: Subject to their mental alertness.
choices.zh: 取决于他们的精神警觉性。

choices.text: Dependent on their analytical ability.
choices.zh: 取决于他们的分析能力。

items.stem: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?

choices.text: Looking the speaker in the eye.
choices.zh: 直视说话者的眼睛。

choices.text: Listening carefully to the speaker.
choices.zh: 仔细倾听说话者。

choices.text: Measuring the speaker's breathing rate.
choices.zh: 测量说话者的呼吸频率。

choices.text: Focusing on the speaker's facial expressions.
choices.zh: 关注说话者的面部表情。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?

choices.text: They don't treat patients with due respect.
choices.zh: 它们没有以应有的尊重对待病人。

choices.text: They witness a lot of doctor-patient conflicts.
choices.zh: 它们目睹了许多医患冲突。

choices.text: They have to deal with social workers' strikes.
choices.zh: 它们必须应对社会工作者的罢工。

choices.text: They don't care how much patients have to pay.
choices.zh: 它们不关心病人要支付多少钱。

items.stem: What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do?

choices.text: Appear submissive and grateful to doctors and nurses.
choices.zh: 在医生和护士面前表现得顺从和感激。

choices.text: Express a strong desire to be consulted or informed.
choices.zh: 表达希望被咨询或告知的强烈愿望。

choices.text: Refrain from saying anything that sounds negative.
choices.zh: 避免说任何听起来负面的话。

choices.text: Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses.
choices.zh: 记下所有医生和护士的名字。

items.stem: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?

choices.text: Cooperative.
choices.zh: 合作的。

choices.text: Appreciative.
choices.zh: 感激的。

choices.text: Passive.
choices.zh: 被动的。

choices.text: Responsive.
choices.zh: 有回应的。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?

choices.text: Its members work together despite risks of failure.
choices.zh: 其成员尽管面临失败风险仍共同协作。

choices.text: It prioritizes recruiting young energetic members.
choices.zh: 它优先招募年轻有活力的成员。

choices.text: Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.
choices.zh: 其成员即使在团队解散后也保持联系。

choices.text: It grows more and more mature professionally.
choices.zh: 它在专业上变得越来越成熟。

items.stem: What do the researchers find out about members of a team?

choices.text: Their differences are likely to impact productivity.
choices.zh: 他们的差异可能会影响生产力。

choices.text: Their similarity is conducive to future collaboration.
choices.zh: 他们的相似性有利于未来的合作。

choices.text: Their connections strengthen with the passage of time.
choices.zh: 他们的联系随着时间推移而加强。

choices.text: Their mutual understanding stems from a common goal.
choices.zh: 他们的相互理解源于共同目标。

items.stem: What do we learn about the team the speaker is currently working in?

choices.text: It is characterized by diversity.
choices.zh: 它的特点是多样性。

choices.text: Its goals are quite inconsistent.
choices.zh: 它的目标相当不一致。

choices.text: Its members have similar backgrounds.
choices.zh: 其成员有相似的背景。

choices.text: It is connected by a unique mechanism.
choices.zh: 它通过一种独特的机制联结在一起。

items.stem: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?

choices.text: Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.
choices.zh: 将收入的百分之二十存起来。

choices.text: Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy.
choices.zh: 预期自己会变富而消费。

choices.text: Living off a small proportion of one's income.
choices.zh: 靠收入的一小部分生活。

choices.text: Saving as much as one can possibly manage.
choices.zh: 尽可能多地储蓄。

items.stem: How does confidence help people to be thrifty?

choices.text: It empowers them to cope with irrational emotions.
choices.zh: 它使他们有能力应对非理性情绪。

choices.text: It will guarantee the profits from their investments.
choices.zh: 它将保证他们的投资获利。

choices.text: It will turn them into successful financial planners.
choices.zh: 它将把他们变成成功的理财规划师。

choices.text: It enables them to focus on long-term investments.
choices.zh: 它使他们能够专注于长期投资。

items.stem: How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment?

choices.text: They count on others to take the responsibility.
choices.zh: 他们指望别人承担责任。

choices.text: They change their investment strategy in time.
choices.zh: 他们及时改变投资策略。

choices.text: They think they themselves are to blame.
choices.zh: 他们认为自己应该受到责备。

choices.text: They persist rather than get discouraged.
choices.zh: 他们坚持下去而不是气馁。

items.stem: Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent?

choices.text: They do not resist novel lifestyles.
choices.zh: 他们不抗拒新颖的生活方式。

choices.text: They do not try to keep up with others.
choices.zh: 他们不试图跟上他人。

choices.text: They do not care what they have acquired.
choices.zh: 他们不在乎自己获得了什么。

choices.text: They do not pressure themselves to get rich.
choices.zh: 他们不给自己施加变富的压力。
